No high or medium defect found in the sizing arithmetic of /home/user/test-trading/trader/tools/entry_v18.py. For today's inputs (E 82.9-88.4, NVDL ask 21.00-23.50, last within 4 cents of the ask) the tool produces the orders that RULES_v3 §3(c), §3(e), §4 and §13(b) require. All eight findings are low: edge cases, missing guards and misleading prints.

Results against the invariants:
- (a) Core quantity: over every E in cents 55.00-130.00 and every ask in cents 14.00-32.00, up and down (27,018,602 cases), the script never gives one share too many. It gives one too few in 73 cases, all exact ties 0.98*E == q*lim in state up; none has E 80-95 with ask 19-24.
- (b) Limit: exact for every cent ask from 14.00 to 32.00 and for 400,000 random 4-decimal asks; ask 20.00 gives 20.03, not 20.04. The only artefacts are 16 asks between 1.07 and 1.22.
- (c) Cap: a violation aborts with an AssertionError and writes nothing. It needs last 5 cents below the ask (ask up to 22.99) or 6 cents (ask 23.00-23.50); the 7 journalled entry quote pairs had gaps of 2 cents or less.
- (d) Top-up: about 3.06 million up/down cases, including exact-cent boundaries one 0.0001 tick either side, match the exact floor to the cent. The 2.00 threshold is right, and spent + amount never exceeds f*E.
- (e) Pause: always exactly 1 share, and topup refuses under pause.
- (f) a = 0: core prints x0, exits 0 and writes nothing; `topup ... E 0 down` then writes the top-up intent. Nothing blocks it.
- (g) Parsing: a missing argument, a state typo, a wrong mode and most swapped orders fail before any write; upper-case state is accepted. Negative or zero numbers and mistyped flags are not caught (findings 4 and 5).
- (h) Intent lines: core has the same keys as the historical lines (NVDL, buy, qty, limit, gfd, regular_hours); the top-up has dollar_amount, market, gfd, regular_hours. Both map onto the broker order schema's fields. dollar_amount is written as a JSON number (2.0 for $2.00), while the schema takes a string.

Today's scenarios, run on the repo script with --dry:
- DOWN, E 87.70: ask up to 21.88 gives 1 share and no top-up; ask 21.89 or higher gives 0 shares, then a 21.92 top-up.
- UP, E 87.70: ask up to 21.45 gives 4 shares; above that, 3 shares plus a top-up of about 21.
- PAUSE: 1 share.

One thing I could not check here: a dollar-based market order's fill cost is computed by the broker from the last trade price, so the claim that spent + amount stays within 0.98*E holds for the order amount, not necessarily to the cent for the fill.

RULES_v3 §4 only says '(<= last*1.004)'; the retired RULES.md X-3 wording was 'never > last x 1.004', i.e. a cap on the price. Neither text says whether to clamp, re-quote or skip. Measured threshold: for ask 21.00-22.99 the assert fires when last is 5 cents or more below the ask, for ask 23.00-23.50 at 6 cents (22-26 bp); any gap of 4 cents or less passes. The 7 entries with a journalled ask/last pair (10/30 to 11/9) had gaps of 2 cents or less, so with a normal 1-3 cent spread it does not fire.
unverified.failure_scenario: `python3 trader/tools/entry_v18.py core 45 20261110 21.50 21.45 86.30 up --dry` -> 'AssertionError: limit 21.54 > last*1.004 21.5358', exit 1, no output. The same happens with 21.90 / 21.84. At 15:52 the operator gets no quantity and no limit and must improvise under the 15:55 / 15:58 deadlines.
unverified.suggested_fix: For today: if it fires, take a fresh quote and re-run; nothing was written, so a re-run is safe. Later: replace the assert with an explicit message and exit code, or clamp (lim = min(lim, floor_cent(last*1.004)) with a WARNING), and add one sentence to §4 saying which behaviour is intended.

unverified.title: Core quantity is one share short when 0.98*E equals q*lim exactly
unverified.claim: `q = int(target // lim)` on binary floats loses the exact-equality case in state up. On the exhaustive cent grid (E 55.00-130.00, ask 14.00-32.00) there are 180 exact ties 0.98*E == q*lim, and 73 of them return q-1. It never returns one too many, and state down (f = 0.25, exact in binary) has no mismatch. A tie needs E to be a multiple of 0.50; none of the 73 has E 80-95 with ask 19-24, so today is not affected.
unverified.failure_scenario: `core 45 20261110 27.39 27.39 84.00 up --dry` prints 'lim 27.44 x2 = 54.88 -> planned top-up 27.43', although 3 x 27.44 = 82.32 = 0.98 x 84.00, so §3(c) gives a = 3. Also E 85.00 / ask 16.63 gives x4 instead of x5. The missing share is then bought by the market top-up instead of the limit order; total exposure is about the same.
unverified.suggested_fix: `q = int((target + 1e-9) // lim)`, the same epsilon line 45 already uses. Verified on the full 27,018,602-case grid: 0 mismatches, no one-more cases. Integer cents would also work.

unverified.title: topup cannot see the core's outcome: SPENT=0 in state up, or a second run, writes a market-buy intent
unverified.claim: The top-up mode trusts SPENT and has no cross-check against the night's core intent. §3(c) says the top-up is 'never if the core was cancelled unfilled' and is ONE order. The script cannot tell 'a = 0' from 'core never filled', and it does not notice an earlier top-up intent for the same night. The assert on line 48 only checks spent + amt <= 0.98*E using the SPENT it was given.
unverified.failure_scenario: `topup 45 20261110 87.70 0 up` (scratch copy, no --dry) wrote an intent with dollar_amount 85.94, market, although a = 0 is impossible in state up at these prices. Running topup again with the same arguments writes another line with the same coid T3X-20261110-45-NVDL-EF and a new ref_id; on a DOWN a = 0 night two such orders would both fit in cash (2 x 21.9, about 50% of E). On a DOWN night with 1 share filled, passing SPENT 0 by mistake writes a second 21.9 buy.
unverified.suggested_fix: In topup, read orders.jsonl for the night: refuse if a -EF line already exists, and refuse SPENT = 0 when a core -E intent with qty >= 1 exists, unless an explicit flag such as --core-zero is given. At the least, refuse SPENT = 0 in state up while 0.98*E would buy a whole share.

unverified.title: Numeric arguments are not sanity-checked; negative or zero values reach the intent line
unverified.claim: Lines 24 and 42 parse floats with no sign or range check, and line 35 only stops on q == 0. A missing argument, a state typo, a wrong mode and most swapped orders do fail loudly before any write (verified); upper-case state is accepted. Negative or zero numbers do not. E <= 50 (KILL) is also sized normally.
unverified.failure_scenario: Scratch copy without --dry: `core 45 20261110 21.60 21.59 -87.70 up` wrote qty -4 at 21.64. `core ... 0 21.59 87.70 up` (ask 0, e.g. a one-sided quote) wrote qty 4297 at limit 0.02. `core ... 2.16 21.59 87.70 up` (ask typo) wrote qty 39 at 2.19. `topup 45 20261110 87.70 -5 up` wrote dollar_amount 90.94, above E, and the 0.98*E assert on line 48 passed. `core ... 21.60 21.59 49.00 up` wrote 2 shares below the KILL level.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add before any write: core `assert ask > 0 and last > 0 and E > 0 and q >= 0`, plus a sanity bound such as 0.5*last <= ask <= 1.5*last; topup `assert E > 0 and 0 <= spent <= 0.98*E`. Optionally refuse E <= 50 with a KILL message.

unverified.title: Unknown flags are silently dropped, so a mistyped --dry writes a live intent line
unverified.claim: Line 16 removes every argument starting with '--' and sets dry only on the exact string '--dry'. Any other spelling is ignored and the run is live.
unverified.failure_scenario: Scratch copy: `core 45 20261110 21.60 21.59 87.70 up --dry-run`, the same with `--DRY`, and the same with `-dry` each appended a qty 3 / limit 21.64 intent line. In the repo this would add an orphan INV-12 line to trader/orders.jsonl during a rehearsal.
unverified.suggested_fix: Reject unknown options: collect arguments that start with '-' and are not numbers; if any is not exactly '--dry', exit with an error before doing anything.

unverified.title: Core print can mislead: target rounded to 2 decimals, planned top-up computed from the limit without the epsilon
unverified.claim: Display only; the orders are right. (1) The target is printed with .2f, so a target of 21.925 shows as 21.93 next to 'lim 21.93 x0', which looks like a sizing error. (2) Line 32 floors without the +1e-9 that line 45 uses, so the planned top-up is one cent below the exact value in about 3% of cases for E 86-88 and ask 21.00-22.59. (3) The '(below 2.00: none)' tag is computed from q*lim, not the fill; with a fill at the ask the real top-up from topup mode is >= 2.00 in about 0.9% of state-up cases in today's band. (4) The header comment on line 10 cites §13(c) for the review_equity_order step; the rule is §13(h).
unverified.failure_scenario: `core 45 20261110 21.89 21.88 87.70 down --dry` prints 'target 21.93 ... lim 21.93 x0 = 0.00 -> planned top-up 21.92'. `core 45 20261110 21.46 21.45 87.75 up --dry` prints 'target 86.00 ... lim 21.50 x3 = 64.50' although 4 x 21.50 = 86.00 (the real target is 85.995). E 83.68, ask 20.00, up: core says 'planned top-up 1.88 (below 2.00: none)', but after a fill at 20.00 topup gives 2.00 and places it. An operator who trusts the core line and skips the topup call misses that order.
unverified.suggested_fix: Print the target with 4 decimals; add + 1e-9 inside the floor on line 32; reword the tag to 'below 2.00 at the limit; run topup after the fill'; change the comment to §13(h). Operationally: always run topup after the core fill, whatever the core line says.

unverified.title: No tool path for the §4 re-price at 15:55 (ask + 0.3%)
unverified.claim: §4 says 'Unfilled at 15:55: re-price once to ask + 0.3%'. The script has only the ask + max(0.02, 0.15%) formula and no re-price mode, whereas exit_ovn.py has --reprice with its own coid suffix. Re-running `core` would price at +0.15%, recompute q from the new limit and write a second intent with the same coid T3X-<day>-<n>-NVDL-E and a new ref_id. This gap already existed in entry_v15/v16, and no entry re-price appears in the journal.
unverified.failure_scenario: Core limit for 3 shares placed at 15:52 does not fill by 15:55. The operator has no command that produces the +0.3% limit and its intent line, and must hand-write both, or re-run core and get the wrong offset with a duplicate coid, with the top-up deadline at 15:58.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add a `--reprice` option to core: lim = ceil_cent(ask*1.003), same q as the original order, coid suffix -E2, mirroring exit_ovn.py. Otherwise document in tools/README.md that the entry re-price intent is written by hand.

unverified.title: In a 4-cent ask window the top-up buys slightly more than 1 share, leaving a dust remainder for the exit
unverified.claim: This follows the rule as written, but the operator should expect it. Because the limit is about 4 cents above the ask, there is a window where (a+1)*ask <= T < (a+1)*lim: the core takes a shares and the dollar top-up then buys 1.000 to about 1.002 shares at the ask. On a DOWN night with a = 0 the 'top-up-only' position is then not under 1 share. In the end-to-end grid (E 82.50-88.50, ask 20.00-23.50, fill at the ask) this happened in 1.1% of DOWN and 1.1% of UP cases. Whether the broker accepts a market sell of about 0.001 share was not checked (no broker access).
unverified.failure_scenario: DOWN, E 86.30 (T 21.575): ask 21.54-21.57 gives lim 21.58-21.61, so core gives x0; topup gives 21.57, which at an ask of 21.54 is 1.001393 shares. With E 87.70 the window is ask 21.89-21.92 (21.92 / 21.89 = 1.00137 shares). Next morning `exit_frac.py 45 <day> NVDL 1.001393` fails its 0 < QTY < 1 assert; the exit must be exit_ovn.py for 1 share, then exit_frac.py for 0.001393 (about 3 cents).
unverified.suggested_fix: No change needed for tonight. Note in the entry journal line when the top-up fill is >= 1 share, and at the exit read the position first: whole part through exit_ovn.py, remainder through exit_frac.py. If dust sells turn out to be a problem, a later rule tweak could use 1 whole share by limit when ask <= T < lim.

unverified.title: Exact tie P == L is usually classified DOWN because of float summation error; rounded output shows price equal to flip with DOWN
unverified.claim: §13(a) says P >= L is UP. Line 89 computes L as a plain float sum of 199 closes divided by 199, and line 90 compares p >= flip on raw floats. For the real QQQ window the float result sits about 1e-13 to 2e-13 above the exact mean, so when the exact mean is a cent value and P equals it, the comparison is False. Separately, flip is printed to 3 decimals and logged to 4, so a price just below the true flip prints as equal with state DOWN.
unverified.failure_scenario: 20,000 synthetic 199-close windows built from the cached QQQ closes, each adjusted so the exact mean is a two-decimal price P: the tool's arithmetic returned DOWN in 14,796 of them. End-to-end on the scratch copy: four closes changed (2026-02-12 599.01, 2026-05-26 729.05, 2026-06-23 714.98, 2026-11-09 679.08) so the exact mean is 681.44; `state QQQ=681.44 --date 2026-11-10` prints 'price 681.440  flip 681.440 ... dist -0.00%  -> DOWN', rc 0. A real tie needs the sum of the 199 closes in cents to be divisible by 199 (1 day in 199) and P to land on that exact cent, so it is very unlikely on any given day. Display case with the real cache: `state QQQ=681.449` prints 'price 681.449  flip 681.449 ... -> DOWN' and logs 'QQQ,681.4490,681.4490,-0.000,DOWN'. The true flip is 681.44905, so the state is right, but it reads as a broken tie in an audit.
unverified.suggested_fix: Compare in exact arithmetic, for example integer cents: round(p*10000)*199 >= sum(round(close*10000)), or use fractions.Fraction or decimal.Decimal built from the strings. Print the threshold explicitly as the lowest cent price that is UP ('UP at or above 681.45') and log flip with 6 decimals.

unverified.title: --log writes rows for an invalid state with no flag, writes no QQQ row when the cache is short, and appends duplicates on a re-run
unverified.claim: The row is appended to `rows` at line 95 even when the QQQ state has just been declared stale (rc = 2), and lines 104-109 log every row. The CSV has no column for validity, warning, exit code or the f actually used. When QQQ cannot be computed (short cache) no QQQ row is written at all, though shadow rows are. Every call with --log appends, so a rehearsal or a second read on the same day leaves two rows for one date with nothing marking which was binding. log.csv is the §13(e) shadow record audited at the quarterly review.
unverified.failure_scenario: Scratch copy with 11/09 removed, `state QQQ=681.30 --date 2026-11-11 --log`. The tool prints 'BINDING QQQ: NO VALID STATE ... size DOWN (f = 0.25)' and exits 2, but log.csv gets '2026-11-11,<utc>,QQQ,681.3000,681.1782,0.018,UP'. The log says UP for a night the rule sized DOWN. Running state with --log twice on 2026-11-10 (QQQ=679.35, then QQQ=681.449) left two QQQ rows for the same date.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add columns valid (0/1), f_used and note (warning text) and always write a QQQ row, with state NONE when it cannot be computed. Either refuse a second --log for the same date and symbol without --force, or document that the last row for a date is the binding one.

unverified.title: state does not validate P and silently ignores `--date=YYYY-MM-DD`
unverified.claim: Line 75 recognises only the two-token form `--date YYYY-MM-DD`. kv() (line 42) skips anything starting with '--', so `--date=2026-11-05` is dropped without error and today's date is used. P is taken as any float (line 43, used at line 90) with no sanity check against the last cached close.
unverified.failure_scenario: `state QQQ=679.35 --date=2026-11-05` returns JSON with "date": "2026-11-10" and today's flip 681.449, rc 0; with --log that would write a row under the wrong date and window. `state QQQ=0`, `QQQ=-5` and `QQQ=nan` all print '-> DOWN ... f = 0.25' with rc 0, which is the safe direction but reported as a valid state. `QQQ=inf` and `QQQ=1e9` print '-> UP ... f = 0.98' with rc 0. `QQQ=600 QQQ=700` silently uses 700. A pasted wrong-symbol or mis-scaled quote at or above 681.45 would therefore be accepted as UP.
unverified.suggested_fix: Accept both --date forms and validate the date string. Exit 2 with a message when P is not finite, is <= 0, or is more than about 15% away from the last cached close of that symbol, and on duplicate symbols or unknown flags.

unverified.title: Crash paths exit 1, not the documented 2; the cache is rewritten in place (not atomic)
unverified.claim: The header, README and §13(a) define only exit codes 0 and 2. Several realistic failures raise an uncaught exception and exit 1 with a traceback: a non-numeric or empty price, QQQ missing or given without '=', `--date` without a value, and a cache file that is not valid JSON. save() opens closes.json with mode 'w' and dumps into it (line 37), so an interrupted add leaves a truncated file. A truncated cache then produces exit 1, while a missing cache file correctly gives exit 2.
unverified.failure_scenario: Scratch: closes.json truncated to 9,000 bytes, `state QQQ=679.35` ends in json.decoder.JSONDecodeError, rc 1; an empty file gives the same. `state NVDA=178.5 SMH=487` gives AssertionError 'QQQ=price is required', rc 1. `state QQQ=abc` gives ValueError, rc 1. A run that keys the fail-safe strictly on 'exit code 2' has no documented instruction for rc 1.
unverified.suggested_fix: Wrap cmd_state in try/except that prints 'NO VALID STATE: <error> -> size DOWN (f = 0.25)' and exits 2. Write the cache to a temporary file in the same directory and os.replace() it. Add one line to the docs: any non-zero exit means no valid state.

unverified.title: No tool checks for an existing intent, and on DOWN nights the broker no longer blocks a repeated buy
unverified.claim: The client order ids are distinct per order kind and night (-E, -EF, -X, -X2, -XF), but the tools never look in orders.jsonl for an existing coid and each run creates a fresh random ref_id. Verified: running `core` twice and `exit_frac.py` twice each logged two lines with the same coid and different ref_ids. entry_v18.py also has no mode for the §4 15:55 re-price; re-running `core` reuses the -E coid and prices at ask + 0.15%, not + 0.3%.
unverified.failure_scenario: Under v1.6 the account was 88% to 98% invested after the entry, so a repeated buy bounced for lack of buying power. On a v1.8 DOWN night about 75% of cash stays free. Example: the worker restarts at 15:52:20 after the DOWN order (1 share, or the $21.57 dollar buy) was submitted but before state.json was written. The backstop operator sees today.entry_done = false, runs `core` or `topup` again, gets a new ref_id and submits. The broker accepts it, and the night is held at about 50% of E instead of 25%. This requires the operator to skip the position check.
unverified.suggested_fix: Before logging, have entry_v18.py, exit_frac.py and exit_ovn.py scan orders.jsonl for the coid; if it is present, print the existing line and exit non-zero unless `--force` is given. Add a `--reprice` mode to `core` with coid suffix -E2 and limit ask + 0.3%.

unverified.title: exit_ovn.py crashes on any quantity that is not a bare integer
unverified.claim: `q=int(q)` raises ValueError for a fractional or zero-padded quantity. README line 5 gives the usage as `SYM:QTY:BID` without saying QTY must be the whole-share part.
unverified.failure_scenario: Tomorrow at 09:31:05 after an UP entry (3 shares plus a $20.97 top-up, about 3.99 shares), `exit_ovn.py 45 20261111 NVDL:3.997642:21.30` gives `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '3.997642'`. The same happens for NVDL:1.0153, NVDL:0.997642 and NVDL:3.00000000. No intent line is written, so it fails safe, but the operator loses time at the exit and has to work out the split by hand.
unverified.suggested_fix: Parse QTY with Decimal, sell floor(QTY) whole shares, and print the exit_frac.py command for the remainder. If floor(QTY) is 0, print "position under 1 share: use exit_frac.py". State the whole-share rule in README line 5.

unverified.title: exit_frac.py rejects a zero-padded quantity
unverified.claim: The check counts characters after the decimal point, not significant decimals. RULES_v3 §5 (line 27) tells the operator to pass "the exact quantity from get_equity_positions". Nothing in the repository records how the broker prints a fractional quantity, and I could not check it.
unverified.failure_scenario: `exit_frac.py 45 20261111 NVDL 0.99764200 --dry` gives `AssertionError: at most 6 decimals`; `0.9976420` fails the same way. If the broker pads quantities to 8 places, the first fractional exit stops on this assertion right after the whole shares have sold, and the remainder (up to about $21, a quarter of E on a DOWN night) sits until the operator re-types it. §7 asks only for "0 open orders" after the exit, so a zero-position check is not required by the text.
unverified.suggested_fix: Normalise with Decimal(q).normalize() and reject only if more than 6 significant decimals remain; write the normalised string to the intent line. Add "position quantity 0" to the post-exit check in RULES_v3 §5 and §7.

unverified.title: trend.py does not detect one to three missing sessions or a hole in the cache
unverified.claim: Exit code 2 is returned only when fewer than 199 closes exist or the last cached close is more than 4 calendar days old. A missed 07:45 `trend.py add` produces a WARNING and exit code 0. A missing date inside the window is never reported. README line 7 and RULES_v3 §13(a) describe exit code 2 as covering a "stale" cache. The `add` step itself is not in the RULES_v3 §0 phase list and not anywhere in state.json.
unverified.failure_scenario: Scratch run with the cache ending 11/9: `state QQQ=681.30 --date 2026-11-13` (three sessions missing) computes a state with a warning and rc 0; rc 2 appears only at a 7-day gap. With the 11/6 close removed, `state QQQ=681.30 --date 2026-11-10` returns UP (flip 681.295) with no warning, while the intact cache returns DOWN (flip 681.449). Each missing session moves the flip by about 0.04%, so the state is wrong only when QQQ is that close to the line; it was 0.27% away on 11/9.
unverified.suggested_fix: Return exit code 2 when the last cached close is not the previous trading day (keep a short NYSE holiday list in the tool, or require an explicit `--allow-gap`). Warn when the 199-close window spans more weekdays than closes plus known holidays. Add "07:45: trend.py add <prior session date>" to the RULES_v3 §0 ANALYST phase.

unverified.title: RULES_v3 §3 and §6 still carry pre-v1.8 sizing text and a stale PAUSE trigger
unverified.claim: The v1.8 commit left three passages untouched that contradict §3(c), §3(d) and §13. Line 17: "Hold the top 2 eligible DISTINCT underlyings, 1 share each ... Target 70-100% of E invested ... add whole shares of #1 one at a time while total cost stays <= 0.98*E ... a lower-priced eligible product on the SAME underlying as #1 (e.g. NVDX for NVDL) may be added as a partial unit". Line 19: "Blackout: skip an instrument on the night its underlying reports earnings ...; substitute next-ranked name". Line 30 (§6): "Now 107.11 (10/12) -> trigger 85.69 until 10/12 leaves the window (~11/9)".
unverified.failure_scenario: On a DOWN night the position is 25% of E. A fresh operator reading §3 top-down meets "Target 70-100% of E invested" and the NVDX partial-unit clause before reaching (c), and could add whole shares or NVDX to repair the size. On 11/17, line 19 says to substitute the next-ranked name where §3(d) says cash. If today's exit leaves E between 82.94 and 85.69, the §6 figure would wrongly read as PAUSE; state.json and STATUS.md give 82.94 today and 82.89 from 11/11.
unverified.suggested_fix: Mark the first paragraph of §3 and the "substitute next-ranked name" clause as superseded by §3(b) to (e), as was done for the v1.6 clause inside (c). Replace the §6 figure with a pointer to state.campaign.pause_schedule.

unverified.title: state.json still describes the v1.6 basket and a September ranking
unverified.claim: campaign.ranking.basket (line 344) reads "v1.6: NVDA-2x core, NVDL first then NVDX filler; no satellite; §3(f) W120 edge-decay switch (Mondays)". The top-level `ranking` block (lines 883 to 1030, asof 2026-09-28) still lists picks [METU, AAPU] with qty 1 each. state.json is the first file every wake reads.
unverified.failure_scenario: A fresh operator sees "NVDL first then NVDX filler" and "picks METU, AAPU" alongside campaign.sizing (v1.8, NVDL only). The correct blocks exist and the entry tool only buys NVDL, so the risk is a hand-placed NVDX filler order when cash is left over on a DOWN night.
unverified.suggested_fix: Change campaign.ranking.basket to the v1.8 wording (NVDL only, f×E, top-up, NVDX not bought). Mark the top-level `ranking` block as historical or move it to the archive.

unverified.title: PAUSE can force a larger position than the DOWN size it is supposed to sit below
unverified.claim: §3(e) (line 18) says PAUSE is "exactly 1 share of NVDL, no top-up, whatever the §13 trend state". §13(b) (line 77) ranks PAUSE above §13 f and adds "§13 never overrides a smaller size". When one share costs more than 0.25×E, the DOWN size is the smaller one, yet PAUSE imposes the whole share. entry_v18.py line 29 implements the 1 share.
unverified.failure_scenario: Verified at E 82.50 and ask 21.20, the situation if today's exit triggers PAUSE at 82.94: `core ... down` gives size 0 and a $20.62 dollar buy (25.0% of E); `core ... pause` gives 1 share at 21.24 (25.7% of E). The gap is small at these prices but widens if E falls faster than NVDL; at E 55 and NVDL 21 the PAUSE share is 38% of E against 25% for DOWN.
unverified.suggested_fix: Decide and write one rule, for example "PAUSE = min(1 share, the §13 size)", and make the pause branch of entry_v18.py follow it. Otherwise delete "never overrides a smaller size" from §13(b) and state that PAUSE is 1 share even when that exceeds 0.25×E.

unverified.title: §13(a) fixes the trend state at 15:50, after the close on half-days
unverified.claim: §13(a) says "at 15:50 ET on every entry day run tools/trend.py state", and §0 gives the same sequence. §4 (line 24) moves the entry to 12:52 on half-days (2026-11-27 and 2026-12-24) "with the same mechanics" and does not mention the trend state. STATUS.md line 49 does not either.
unverified.failure_scenario: On Fri 11/27 the one-off wake fires at 12:44. `entry_v18.py core` needs up, down or pause at 12:52, but the rule text places the state read at 15:50, after the 13:00 close. A fresh operator must improvise, either skipping the state and guessing a size or reusing the previous day's state.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add to §13(a) and to the §4 half-day paragraph: "on half-days the state is read at 12:50 ET".

unverified.title: LAB.md L5 and RULES_v3 §3(b) set different bars for adding a second name
unverified.claim: LAB.md L5 pre-registers: "a blend beats NVDA-2x on g in both halves of 2015–26 and on the real-ETF period" for blends with SOXL or TQQQ, judged 2027-01-11. RULES_v3 §3(b) (line 18) says a second name may be proposed only "on executable 15:52->09:31 prices, ex-earnings both sides, avg volume >= 1M, and a score lead >= 0.06 over the core at two consecutive Monday re-ranks".
unverified.failure_scenario: At the 2027-01-11 review a blend could pass the L5 test without meeting the §3(b) score-lead and executable-price conditions, or the reverse. The lab run would then have two conflicting pre-registered criteria for the same decision.
unverified.suggested_fix: Make L5's pass criteria state that §3(b) must also be met, or amend §3(b) to name the L5 test as the governing criterion. Pick one before the review.
